packet.headline_seed: DeepMind CEO calls for an independent standards body to regulate frontier AI
packet.description_seed: DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis is proposing an AI "standards body" modeled after FINRA, to test frontier models and develop best practices for their release.

what: DeepMind CEO calls for an independent standards body to regulate frontier AI

clean_source_blocks.text: DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis is proposing an AI "standards body" modeled after FINRA, to test frontier models and develop best practices for their release.

In an X post on Tuesday morning, Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis called for the creation of a new regulatory body to oversee frontier model releases. Titled “A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age,” the post makes the case for a “standards body” modeled after the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), which could test frontier models and develop best practices for their release.

The DeepMind CEO’s vision for an AI industry regulatory authority would begin with a board of tech experts and open-source representatives funded by the AI industry itself – a move that would “attract world-class technical talent” and ensure the body had enough hardware to run its various frontier model tests. FINRA is funded in a similar manner by the industry it purports to regulate, which has opened the door to criticism that it's basically a toothless insiders' club. Funding and conflict-of-interest concerns aside, the main task of the AI standards body Hassabis proposed would be to establish an assessment protocol for frontier AI models, and to dete

Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, has advocated for the establishment of a U.S. Frontier AI Standards Body to conduct testing of AI models concerning national security before their deployment in the market. This proposal aligns with President Trump’s Executive Order 14409, which initiated a voluntary 30-day pre-release review framework for “covered frontier models.” Hassabis’s suggestion, however, aims to formalize and eventually mandate this review process through a newly proposed regulatory body. This development appears to be potentially influencing Trump’s AI review process, impacting the odds on related prediction markets.

In an X post on Tuesday morning, Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis called for the creation of a new regulatory body to oversee frontier model releases. Titled “A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age,” the post makes the case for a “standards body” modeled after the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), which could test frontier models and develop best practices for their release.

“Initially, Frontier Labs would voluntarily share models with the Standards Body for review up to 30 days before release,” the post reads. “Once the assessment protocol is shown to be effective and robust, formalisation could quickly follow, meaning that Frontier Models would be required to pass it to be deployed in the US market. Labs would also work with the Standards Body to address any critical post-release vulnerabilities.”The proposed system would build on the ad hoc reviews performed by the US government on Anthropic’s Mythos and OpenAI’s Sol. Those reviews drew significant criticism for lack of technical expertise and opaque decision-making as to when a model could be released. Under Hassabis’s proposed regulator, those decisions could be handed off to a new organization, backed by the US government but funded by the AI industry and operated independently.

This development appears to be potentially influencing Trump’s AI review process, impacting the odds on related prediction markets.

The current U.S. framework for AI governance is primarily voluntary, with the CAISI under the Commerce Department conducting evaluations through agreements. Hassabis’s proposal would transition this to a mandatory framework upon the formalization of standards. This move is perceived as aligning with national security priorities, suggesting a moderate shift in market odds regarding the federal review of AI model releases ordered by Trump.

Google DeepMind boss Demis Hassabis is calling for the US to establish a robust frontier AI model review process because, according to him, artificial general intelligence (AGI) “is probably only a few short years away" and we've got to figure it out before it's too late.

That “probably” is doing a lot of heavy lifting in Hassabis’ lengthy, early-morning Tuesday post on X. Like commercially viable fusion power and practical fault-tolerant quantum computing, AGI seems perpetually asymptotic to the present moment, with needed technological advancements always the next step in the process.

No amount of hyperbole - not even a Nobel laureate with skin in the game predicting an impact “perhaps 10x of the Industrial Revolution at 10x the speed” - makes the AGI timetable any more certain. Recall that Hassabis predicted in the beginning of 2025 that human trials of AI-designed drugs would come that year, and that still hasn’t happened either.

payload.title: DeepMindin Demis Hassabis ehdottaa Yhdysvaltoihin tekoälyn standardointielintä
payload.summary: Google DeepMindin toimitusjohtaja Demis Hassabis haluaa uuden elimen arvioimaan edistyneimpiä tekoälymalleja ennen niiden julkaisua. Toimialan rahoittaman elimen riippumattomuus voisi kuitenkin herättää eturistiriitoja.
payload.content:
Google DeepMindin toimitusjohtaja Demis Hassabis ehdottaa Yhdysvaltoihin uutta standardointielintä, joka arvioisi edistyneimpiä tekoälymalleja ennen niiden pääsyä markkinoille. Elin testaisi malleja myös kansallisen turvallisuuden näkökulmasta, loisi yhteisen arviointimenettelyn ja valmistelisi parhaita käytäntöjä mallien julkaisemiseen. Hassabis haluaa siirtää nykyisen vapaaehtoisen tarkastelun kohti muodollista ja lopulta pakollista järjestelmää.

## Mallina finanssialan sääntelyelin

Hassabis esitteli ehdotuksen tiistaiaamuna X-palvelussa julkaisemassaan kirjoituksessa, jonka otsikko viittasi eturintaman tekoälyn kehykseen ja uuden aikakauden alkamiseen. Hahmotelman esikuvana on Yhdysvaltain finanssialan sääntelyelin FINRA. Uuden elimen päätehtävänä olisi laatia arviointiprotokolla eturintaman tekoälymalleille. Ehdotus koskee niin kutsuttuja eturintaman malleja eli alan kehittyneimpiä järjestelmiä.

Hassabiksen mallissa toiminta alkaisi hallituksella, jossa olisi teknologia-asiantuntijoita ja avoimen lähdekoodin edustajia. Rahoitus tulisi tekoälytoimialalta itseltään. Hassabiksen mukaan tällainen järjestely auttaisi houkuttelemaan maailmanluokan teknistä osaamista ja varmistaisi, että elimellä olisi käytössään riittävästi laitteistoa erilaisten eturintaman mallien testaamiseen. Elimen olisi pystyttävä suorittamaan useita omia mallikokeita, mikä tekee laskentaresursseista olennaisen osan ehdotusta.

## Vapaaehtoisesta arvioinnista pakolliseen malliin

Ehdotus liittyy presidentti Trumpin toimeenpanomääräykseen 14409, jolla käynnistettiin vapaaehtoinen 30 päivän ennakkoarviointimenettely määräyksen piiriin kuuluville eturintaman malleille. Nykyinen kehys perustuu siis vapaaehtoisuuteen. Hassabiksen ehdottama yhdysvaltalainen standardointielin tekisi tarkastelusta muodollisemman ja keskittäisi mallien arvioinnin sitä varten perustetulle toimijalle.

Tarkastusten kohteena olisivat erityisesti mallien kansalliseen turvallisuuteen liittyvät ominaisuudet ennen kuin mallit tuodaan markkinoille. Hassabiksen tavoitteena on, että ennakkoarvioinnista tulisi ajan mittaan pakollinen. Ehdotus veisi siten nykyistä 30 päivän vapaaehtoista kehystä kohti järjestelmää, jossa uusi elin määrittelisi arviointitavan ja valvoisi sen soveltamista. Samalla elin kehittäisi yhteiset parhaat käytännöt sille, millaisin ehdoin mallit voidaan julkaista.

## Toimialan rahoitukseen liittyy eturistiriitojen riski

Toimialan rahoitus tarjoaisi asiantuntijoita ja laskentaan tarvittavaa laitteistoa, mutta samalla se herättää eturistiriitoja koskevan kysymyksen. Myös FINRA saa rahoituksensa siltä toimialalta, jota sen on tarkoitus säännellä. Mallia on tämän vuoksi arvosteltu hampaattomaksi sisäpiirin kerhoksi. Tekoälyelimen uskottavuuden kannalta ratkaisevaa olisi, miten toimialan rahoitus, hallituksen kokoonpano ja riippumaton mallien arviointi sovitettaisiin yhteen. Esitetty kritiikki kohdistuu juuri rahoittajan ja valvojan väliseen suhteeseen.

DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis is proposing an AI "standards body" modeled after FINRA, to test frontier models and develop best practices for their release.

In an X post on Tuesday morning, Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis called for the creation of a new regulatory body to oversee frontier model releases. Titled “A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age,” the post makes the case for a “standards body” modeled after the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), which could test frontier models and develop best practices for their release.

The DeepMind CEO’s vision for an AI industry regulatory authority would begin with a board of tech experts and open-source representatives funded by the AI industry itself – a move that would “attract world-class technical talent” and ensure the body had enough hardware to run its various frontier model tests. FINRA is funded in a similar manner by the industry it purports to regulate, which has opened the door to criticism that it's basically a toothless insiders' club. Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, has advocated for the establishment of a U.S. Frontier AI Standards Body to conduct testing of AI models concerning national security before their deployment in the market. This proposal aligns with President Trump’s Executive Order 14409, which initiated a voluntary 30-day pre-release review framework for “covered frontier models.” Hassabis’s suggestion, however, aims to formalize and eventually mandate this review process through a newly proposed regulatory body. This development appears to be potentially influencing Trump’s AI review process, impacting the odds on related prediction markets.
